channel.description: Latest articles from B Square Bulletin (bsquarebulletin.com)

item.title: Morton Street & 6th Street
item.description: The sign in the elevator at Morton Street garage says: “Warning: No Jumping, bouncing, or erratic movement. You maybe entrapped.”

item.title: Kirkwood Avenue & Washington Street (Buskirk-Chumley Theater)
item.description: Busking under the canopy of the Buskirk-Chumley Theater this morning are The Monon Troubadours.

item.title: Photos: Pretty birds in a Bloomington park
item.description: On Sunday (March 22) around 11 a.m, Bloomington’s Miller-Showers Park was alive with fancy birds two days into spring under sunny skies with the temperature at 77F° and climbing towards the forecasted high of 84F°. Cardinals, robins, hawks, ducks—what else could you want?

item.title: Civic Solver: March 23, 2026
item.description: This week’s puzzle is an 11-question quiz about the duties and responsibilities of different county elected officials. Please not this is not some basic 10-question quiz. It goes all the way to 11!

item.title: March 23, 2026: Hopewell South, election prep, voting, pretty birds
item.description: This edition includes reports on final preparations for the May 5 primary election with early voting starting on April 7. Also in this edition is a preview of the city council’s vote on Hopewell South at its Wednesday meeting.

item.title: After 5 months, ruling still pending from highest court for Bloomington annexation case
item.description: Bloomington’s long-running annexation fight is half over. The city has lost in two west-side areas, while a constitutional case covering five other territories remains pending. A recent U.S. Supreme Court decision could shape an expected ruling soon.

item.title: 6th Street & Washington Street
item.description: Display case at Baked! filled with cookies of all kinds and flavors. Baked! is back after a three-month hiatus due to a water pipe failure.

item.title: Point of contention for Monroe County commissioner candidates: Listening versus results
item.description: At a League of Women Voters forum, Democratic commissioner candidates Trent Deckard and David Henry contrasted styles—collaboration versus results—while debating vote centers, a new jail site, ICE cooperation, and restoring public trust in county government.

item.title: 10th Street & Pete Ellis Drive
item.description: Seven stumps of trees cut down in preparation for an INDOT project. This is looking southwest. In early February, the trees had been marked with white Xs for removal. The city of Bloomington reached an agreement with INDOT to cut down seven instead of 15 trees.

item.title: Monroe County test run clears voting machines for May 5 primary
item.description: Monroe County’s voting machines passed a routine logic and accuracy test using about 4,000 ballots designed to trigger every scenario. Under bipartisan oversight, results matched expected results, clearing a key step ahead of the May 5 primary.
